title: Progressive telemetry-driven output synthesis and SDK cookbook
body:
Summary:
This is a working cookbook for a telemetry-driven progressive output surface combined with pragmatic SDK ergonomics for incremental streaming + tool invocation. Goal is to define a small set of developer-facing patterns that: 1) allow apps to consume partial responses with stable contracts, 2) surface telemetry hooks for quality/cost decisions (early abort, fidelity downgrade, prefetch), and 3) keep SDK usage simple for engineers who don’t want to own complex backoff/fanout logic.

Context and motivation:
- We have many internal PRDs about streaming protocols, typed tool contracts, and progressive frames. Field feedback: customers want easier client-side patterns (sync-first mental model) and predictable billing/latency tradeoffs.
- Observability is the lever: if we expose token-level and event-level telemetry to SDKs, the client can make smarter adaptions (e.g., switch to cheap-model mid-output, abort non-critical branches).
- This doc sketches runtime policies, proto API shapes, SDK ergonomics, and concrete examples for mobile/web/backends.

Core principles (constraints):
- Minimal surface area: two SDK primitives (subscribePartial, finalizeOrCancel) + optional tool-call helper.
- Contract-first: partial responses must be valid prefixes (JSONL lines or frame envelopes) so clients can render confidently.
- Telemetry-first: include per-partial telemetry metadata (modelVariant, latencyMs, tokenBudgetRemaining, qualityScore) in stream frames.
- Failures are explicit: every partial frame includes a status enum (ok | degraded | truncated | error) and optional fallback_hint.

User stories:
- Mobile summary card: receive first 100 tokens quickly (low-cost variant), render a preview; if user taps expand, SDK automatically fetches higher-fidelity continuation or stitches cached prefix with high-fidelity suffix.
- Chat with tool calls: UI stitches tool-call frames inline (toolResult frames) and can optimistically render placeholders while awaiting external tool.
- Backend reranker: consumes incremental candidate embeddings, aborts early if telemetry indicates low expected quality for further tokens.

API/Frame shape (idea):
- envelope: {frame_id, session_id, sequence, kind, payload, meta} (we will keep actual contract small).
- kinds we expect: text_chunk, structured_json, tool_call, tool_result, telemetry_delta, commit_marker
- meta fields (always present): model_variant, tokens_generated, latency_ms, budget_units, quality_est (0-1), status
(Implementation note: body will be newline-separated JSONL frames to simplify client parsing.)

SDK ergonomics (primitives):
1) subscribePartial(request, handlers, opts) -> returns subscription handle
   - handlers: onPartial(frame), onTelemetry(meta), onComplete(summary), onError(err)
   - opts: initial_model_hint, budget_target, max_preview_tokens, fallback_profile_id
   - Behavior: SDK buffers safe prefixes and calls onPartial with each committed frame. It also surfaces telemetry frames separately so UI can attach badges/metrics.

2) finalizeOrCancel(handle, finalMode)
   - finalMode: stitchToVariant | abort | escalateToHighFidelity
   - returns promise that resolves to final commit marker or error

3) toolCall helper: small wrapper that creates an inline tool_call frame and returns a tool_result when ready. Built-in timeouts and retry heuristics backed by telemetry (if tool latency > X, SDK can auto-fallback).

Progressive fallback profiles (runtime):
- fast-preview: low-cost model, short prefix, quality_est threshold 0.4. Good for previews.
- balanced: default; moderate tokens, telemetry-driven hedge to high-fidelity if quality_est < 0.65
- faithful: always use high-fidelity variant, but SDK can stream lower-fidelity previews for very slow networks (telemetry shows mobile bandwidth low).

Telemetry-driven decision examples (recipes):
- Early upgrade: If cumulative quality_est rises above 0.8 and user expands, SDK issues an upgrade request to append higher-fidelity continuation. Server can accept and return a commit_marker that signals a safe stitch point.
- Silent degrade: If backend signals model_variant_evict soon (capacity), SDK substitutes succinct fallback_hint to app and continues with reduced tokens; UI shows 'degraded' badge.
- Cost steering: products can pass budget_target and SDK will throttle prefetch/tool-calls to stay within per-session budget. Telemetry updates let app show remaining budget.

Structured output patterns:
- Schema-anchored frames: structured_json frames always include schema_version and stable field paths; incremental partials must not break top-level fields (i.e., emit field-by-field commits rather than streaming an incomplete top-level object).
- Hybrid mode: For large objects, send a small skeleton structured_json first, then text_chunk frames for narrative content, then final structured_json commit with resolved fields.

Edge cases and compatibility notes:
- Offline resume: subscription handle keeps a short replay log (last N frames). When a client reconnects, it requests resume(session_id, last_seq). Server must be able to replay from cache or regenerate with deterministic seeds to avoid incoherent stitching.
- Cross-variant stitching: server should emit commit_marker with compatibility hints (can_stitch: true/false). SDK must avoid naive concatenation if compatibility is false.
- Tool-call partials: tool_result frames may arrive out-of-order; each has a tool_call_id and sequence; SDK provides a helper to attach placeholder UI nodes keyed by call_id.

Developer UX guide (do/don't):
- DO expose telemetry badges (fast/ok/slow/cost-high) and let product choose graceful degradations.
- DON'T rely on naive token counts for billing indicators; use server budget_units telemetry to show user-facing cost signals.
- DO provide a local simulator (devkit) that can inject latency and degrade quality_est so frontends can test combos.

Operational and observability requirements:
- Per-session telemetry retention: keep 48 hours of detailed token-level telemetry for debugging, aggregated 90d.
- Alerts: spike in truncated frames (>1%) should trigger SRE paging (indicator of capacity pressure or model OOM).
- Sandbox mode: SDK devkits should be able to toggle telemetry verbosity and simulate fallback profiles.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How granular should telemetry be? Per-token emits are rich but high-volume; per-frame summarization might be the right balance. Need perf experiments.
- Where to place stitch logic? server vs client. Leaning toward server providing compatibility hints and client choosing whether to escalate; server still needs to support deterministic resume.
- Billing UX: show budget in-app? privacy and billing clarity needed.

Next steps / actionable items:
- Run an experiment: implement telemetry_delta frames in runtime and a lightweight SDK handle in web SDK. (Linear HL-342) - owner: Jonah.
- Prototype devkit that simulates: network slowness, model_variant swaps, tool latency. Owner: Maya.
- Design doc for commit_marker contract: define fields can_stitch, stitch_score, canonical_seed. Owner: Priya (this doc).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and SDK-first. Looking for feedback on the minimal primitives set and the telemetry fields that unlock product use-cases.
- If we decide telemetry verbosity is too high-volume, we can gate detailed frames behind an opt-in debug flag per session.

TODOs (short list):
- [ ] Align on envelope schema and send to runtime team for prototyping
- [ ] Draft sample SDK code snippets for web/mobile and embed in developer-lab
- [ ] Add telemetry budget visual mockups for Console

Appendix: quick example (pseudo-JS)
// subscribe, get preview fast, upgrade on expand
const h = await sdk.subscribePartial({prompt, opts:{fallback_profile:'fast-preview', max_preview_tokens:80}}, {
  onPartial: frame => renderChunk(frame.payload),
  onTelemetry: m => renderBadge(m.quality_est, m.latency_ms),
  onComplete: s => console.log('complete', s)
})
// later
await sdk.finalizeOrCancel(h, 'escalateToHighFidelity')

Linked experiments: HL-342, PR #514 (runtime frame support).

---
End of doc.
